record.original_question: Let O_3 be the octahedron graph. A metric space X satisfies O_3-comparison if every labeling of six points x, x', y, y', z, z' in X by the vertices of O_3 admits a model configuration in Hilbert space in which the three diagonal distances xx', yy', zz' do not decrease and all edge lengths do not increase. Does every geodesic CAT(0) space satisfy O_3-comparison?

evidence.quote: Suppose Γ is a graph with vertices v1, . . . , vn. We say that a metric space X meets the Γ-comparison if, for any set of points in X labeled by the vertices of Γ, there is a model configuration ṽ1, . . . , ṽn in the Hilbert space H such that if v_i is adjacent to v_j, then |ṽ_i − ṽ_j|_H ⩽ |v_i−v_j|_X, and otherwise, |ṽ_i−ṽ_j|_H ⩾ |v_i−v_j|_X.

Let us denote by O_3 the graph of the octahedron. For the labeling shown on the diagram, O_3-comparison means that any six-point configuration x, x′, y, y′, z, z′ ∈ X can be mapped to H so that the diagonals xx′, yy′, and zz′ do not get shorter and the edges do not get longer.
Is it true that O_3-comparison holds in any geodesic CAT(0) space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote a separable real Hilbert space. Given a finite simple graph $\Gamma$ with vertex set $\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$, say that a metric space $(X,d_X)$ satisfies $\Gamma$-comparison if for every $n$-tuple of points $p_1,\dots,p_n \in X$ (labeled by the vertices of $\Gamma$) there exists a configuration $\tilde v_1,\dots,\tilde v_n \in \mathcal{H}$ such that
\[
\|\tilde v_i-\tilde v_j\|_{\mathcal{H}} \le d_X(p_i,p_j) \quad\text{whenever } v_iv_j \text{ is an edge of }\Gamma,
\]
and
\[
\|\tilde v_i-\tilde v_j\|_{\mathcal{H}} \ge d_X(p_i,p_j) \quad\text{whenever } v_iv_j \text{ is not an edge of }\Gamma.
\]

Let $O_3$ denote the octahedron graph: the graph on six vertices $x,x',y,y',z,z'$ in which all pairs are joined by an edge except the three "diagonal" pairs $\{x,x'\}$, $\{y,y'\}$, $\{z,z'\}$. Thus $O_3$-comparison for $X$ asserts that every six-point configuration $x,x',y,y',z,z' \in X$ admits a model $\tilde x,\tilde x',\tilde y,\tilde y',\tilde z,\tilde z' \in \mathcal{H}$ in which the three diagonal distances do not decrease while the twelve edge distances do not increase.

Recall that a geodesic metric space $X$ is CAT(0) if every geodesic triangle in $X$ is at least as "thin" as its Euclidean comparison triangle, in the standard sense of Alexandrov.

Question: Does every geodesic CAT(0) space satisfy $O_3$-comparison?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Lebedeva and Petrunin ("Trees meet octahedron comparison", J. Topol. Anal., 2023, arXiv:2212.06445) and the survey "Graph comparison meets Alexandrov" establish $O_3$-comparison for metric trees and their products and prove that $O_3$-comparison implies $C_4$-comparison (which is equivalent to CAT(0)), but the converse — whether every geodesic CAT(0) space satisfies $O_3$-comparison — is explicitly stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Trees meet octahedron comparison
status_evidence.snippet: O_3-comparison implies C_4-comparison; the latter is one of equivalent ways to describe the CAT(0)-comparison. However, C_4-comparison does not imply O_3-comparison.
status_evidence.claim: Whether all CAT(0) spaces satisfy O_3-comparison is recorded as an open problem; only the implication O_3 ⇒ CAT(0) is known.

status_evidence.title: Graph comparison meets Alexandrov — Lebedeva, Petrunin
status_evidence.snippet: A key open question is whether O_3-comparison holds in any complete length CAT(0) space.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as open in the authors' survey on graph comparisons.
